criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale
criteria.reasoning: Clear mission: reef bleaching monitoring for GBR, benefits Australia, identifies users and need. Good context and literature links with in-text citations.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring
would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react

criteria.name: Project plan
criteria.reasoning: Gantt with tasks and deadlines present, tasks explained. Lacks contingency/variation planning and explicit rationale for sources; Useful Links listed separately.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart
Background Research: This research will be ongoing throughout almost the entire design

criteria.name: Preliminary progress
criteria.reasoning: Only literature reading and STK tutorials done. No technical calculations, orbit/launch analysis yet, so preliminary technical content minimal.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner's monitoring system in Hawaii

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Well-structured with headings, good writing, consistent formatting. Gantt readable, references cited and listed matching.

technical_issues.issue: No hand calculations shown for orbit, launch, coverage or link budget despite requirement to supplement software with hand calculations.
Preliminary progress claims only literature review and STK tutorials 1-4, no quantitative space segment design presented.

overall: Mission rationale strong and well referenced. Project plan feasible with Gantt. Weak technical progress, lacking hand calculations and orbit specifics.

feedback.summary: You have a strong, well-referenced mission rationale for GBR monitoring. Your project plan is feasible with a Gantt chart, and your report is well-structured. To progress to Part 2, you need to add quantitative technical work and contingency planning, especially hand calculations for orbits and coverage.

criteria.C1: You clearly defined your reef bleaching mission on p2, linking it to Australian benefit and users like marine scientists. Your literature referencing is strong. To stay at Accomplished, keep this clarity and depth for Part 2.
criteria.C2: You presented a feasible plan with a Gantt Chart on p3 and explained tasks like Background Research on p4. To reach Accomplished, add contingency and variation planning and integrate your source rationale directly into the narrative, not just in Useful Links.
criteria.C3: You have completed literature review and STK tutorials 1-4 on p4, which is good preparation. To reach Accomplished, you need quantitative preliminary results with hand calculations for orbit, launch, coverage and link budget to supplement STK, as missing on p4.
criteria.C4: Your report on p2-p3 with headings Mission Concept & Rationale and Project Plan is clear, well-written and consistently formatted with matching citations. Maintain this standard for Part 2.

next_steps: On p4, add 1-2 pages of hand calculations for a sun-synchronous orbit, revisit coverage, and link budget to complement STK results.
Revise your p3 Gantt plan to include 2 weeks buffer for STK/Orbit iteration and define contingency if launch options change.
Integrate your source list into the methodology on p4 by justifying why Asner Hawaii and specific STK tutorials inform your payload choice.
